content_preview.title: Grafana 13.2 Ships Saved Queries, GitHub Enterprise Git Sync, and a New View Panel Sidebar
content_preview.summary: Grafana 13.2 brings a generally available shared query library, Git Sync support for GitHub Enterprise and webhook-based GitLab/BitBucket sync, and a public-preview view panel sidebar for viewers.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Grafana Labs released Grafana 13.2 on August 20, 2026, adding a generally available shared query library called saved queries, expanded Git Sync support for GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, and BitBucket, and a new view panel sidebar that lets viewers explore dashboard data without edit permissions, according to [Grafana Labs](https://grafana.com/blog/grafana-13-2-release-all-the-latest-features?pg=blog). The release is tagged v13.2.0 on the project's GitHub repository and includes a fix ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News-category piece (553 words, within the 400-1200 range). Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Background structure is followed correctly. Sentences attribute claims consistently to the correct source per statement rather than blanket-citing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and snapshot sha256 hashes were independently recomputed from the gzipped files and matched manifest.json exactly (source-0.html.gz: c6c752d7f24a...66f4db2 hash of blog page; source-1.html.gz: e32ee1be6679...9035ce0 hash of GitHub release page). Read both snapshots in full via gunzip + HTML text extraction (not re-WebFetched). source-0 (grafana.com/blog) confirms: saved queries GA in Grafana Cloud/Enterprise with title/description/tags, save from panels/Explore/annotation queries; org-wide browsing with author/tag filters and starring; RBAC for saved queries; Cmd/Ctrl+K command-palette access and Terraform provisioning; Grafana Assistant 'now supports over 30 data sources', free-tier + self-managed availability since Grafana 13; View panel sidebar (public preview, all editions) enabling legend/stacking adjustments and fanout without edit permissions; Git Sync GitHub Enterprise support (Server+Cloud), GitLab/BitBucket webhooks, and the exact quoted phrase 'pairs with commit signing for verified authorship' appears verbatim; redesigned query variable editor, multi-select panel grouping, Workload Identity Federation for BigQuery/Google Cloud Monitoring, and the homepage refresh surfacing firing alerts alongside recent/starred dashboards. source-1 (github.com release page) confirms tag v13.2.0, 'CVE-2026-17183' listed under a 'Security' heading in 'What's new highlights', and Alerting-section entries covering import workflows and notification-template handling. All claims in the article body trace to one of these two snapshots; no unsupported specifics found.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinations detected. Specifically verified the release-date claim in the Overview ('released Grafana 13.2 on August 20, 2026'): the blog snapshot's page metadata carries 'post_date':'2026-08-20 00:00', 'published_at':'2026-08-20T15:04:19Z', a visible byline date of 2026-08-20, and a JSON-LD 'datePublished':'2026-08-20' -- all consistent with August 20, 2026, and the date is attributed to Grafana Labs (the blog), not to GitHub. The GitHub release page separately shows only 'released this 18 Aug 12:48' with no year printed anywhere on the page -- the article correctly does NOT cite this ambiguous, year-less GitHub timestamp as a date, and correctly does not use it to source the Overview's date claim. I searched the full submission JSON for the literal string '2024' (grep) and confirmed zero occurrences -- the fabricated 'August 18, 2024' date mentioned in the bot's PR self-report does not appear anywhere in the final article. The CVE-2026-17183 fix claim is supported (CVE listed under a 'Security' heading on the release page); the article's 'What We Don't Know' section correctly notes the page does not detail the CVE's scope/severity beyond the bare listing, which matches what the snapshot actually contains.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, factual, no editorializing or marketing language beyond direct attributed quotes from the source.
